title: How to Use a Password Manager: A Complete Beginner's Guide
excerpt: Password managers are the single most effective security upgrade you can make today. This guide walks you through choosing one, setting it up, and using it safely from day one.
content:
Why You Need a Password Manager

The average person has over 100 online accounts. Remembering a unique, strong password for each one is impossible — so most people reuse the same handful of passwords everywhere. That's a disaster waiting to happen: when one site gets breached (and they do, constantly), attackers try those leaked credentials on every other site. This is called credential stuffing, and it's responsible for the majority of account takeovers.

A password manager solves this completely. It remembers every password for you, generates new random ones when you sign up for accounts, and autofills them when you log in. You only need to remember one strong master password.

Choosing the Right Password Manager

There are dozens of options, but a few stand out for reliability and security:

  • NordPass — Uses XChaCha20 encryption (newer and faster than AES-256), has a clean interface, and offers a free tier that's genuinely useful. Great for individuals. Try NordPass free.
  • 1Password — The gold standard for families and teams. Its Travel Mode (which hides selected vaults when crossing borders) is a unique feature no competitor offers. Start a 14-day trial.
  • Bitwarden — Open-source and free. If you want to audit exactly how your passwords are protected, the code is publicly available on GitHub.

All three use zero-knowledge architecture, meaning the company cannot read your passwords even if they wanted to. Your vault is encrypted on your device before it ever touches their servers.

Setting Up Your Manager: Step by Step

  1. Download the app and browser extension. Install on your phone and computer. The browser extension is what handles autofill on websites.
  2. Create a strong master password. This is the one password you must memorize. Use our password generator to create one — aim for at least 20 characters, or use a passphrase of 5+ random words (e.g., correct-horse-battery-staple-river).
  3. Write down your master password and store it physically. Put it in a safe, a locked drawer, or give a copy to a trusted family member. If you lose it, you lose everything.
  4. Import existing passwords. Most browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) let you export your saved passwords as a CSV. Your password manager can import this file — check Settings for an Import option.
  5. Enable two-factor authentication on the manager itself. Use an authenticator app like Google Authenticator or Authy, not SMS.

Migrating Your Old Passwords

Once you're set up, start replacing weak and reused passwords. Don't try to do it all at once — you'll burn out. Instead, update passwords as you log in naturally. When you visit a site, if the password manager flags it as weak or reused, change it then. Within a few weeks you'll have replaced most of your important accounts.

Prioritize these first: email accounts, bank and financial accounts, social media, and any account that stores payment information. These are the most valuable to attackers.

Using It Day to Day

Once installed, a password manager fades into the background. When you visit a login page, the browser extension icon will light up — click it to autofill. When you create a new account, use the built-in password generator (set to at least 20 characters, all character types). The manager saves it automatically.

On your phone, enable the password manager as your autofill provider in settings: on iOS, go to Settings → Passwords → AutoFill Passwords. On Android, go to Settings → General Management → Passwords and Autofill.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Storing your master password in the manager itself. If you get locked out, you're stuck.
  • Using a weak master password. The master password is the only thing standing between an attacker and all your other passwords.
  • Not enabling 2FA on the manager. Two-factor authentication on the manager is non-negotiable.
  • Forgetting to lock the manager when others might use your device. Set it to auto-lock after 1-5 minutes of inactivity.

Recommended Tools

Ready to get started? For individuals, NordPass offers the cleanest experience and a free plan that covers most people's needs. For families or teams, 1Password is the most polished option with excellent sharing features. Check out our full recommended security tools page for a detailed comparison.
